11:718: The Beautiful Dreamer line, descending from broodmare Beautiful Dreamer imported before the war, is one of Japan's three great female lines still going today.
In 1908, Koiwai Farm in Iwate bought Beautiful Dreamer from England as a foundation mare for a huge sum, about $5M today.
Since then, many stars came not only from her own foals but from her daughters Taneyoshi and Beautiful Dreamer III.
Taneyoshi's line gave Derby winner Kabutoyama, Haiseiko's rival Take Hope, and his sister, Oaks winner Take Fubuki.
Also great miler Nippo Teio and his sister, QEII Cup winner Talented Girl.
Plus speedy mare Elps and "Fickle George" Erimo George.
Later came 3-time G1 winner T.M. Ocean and Whale Capture, winner of the 2012 Victoria Mile.
The other branch, Beautiful Dreamer III, produced Hakuryo, winner of the Kikuka Sho and Tenno Sho,
Hall of Famer Meiji Hikari and postwar great Shinzan, but it has now almost died out.
11:719: The Flories Cup line is counted among Japan's three great female lines with the Astonishment and Beautiful Dreamer lines.
In 1907, Koiwai Farm in Iwate imported Flories Cup from England as a foundation mare.
Since then, the line produced Garnet, winner of the Tenno Sho and Arima Kinen, Derby winner Matsumidori, double winner Kitano Kachidoki,
Hall of Famer Kodama with 7 straight wins, Derby winner Minami Homare, 4-time G1 winner Meisho Samson, Asahi Hai FS winner Seiun Wonder and more.
The line from Flories Cup mare Shiraoki has also been remarkable, starting with her sons, Hall of Famer Kodama and Satsuki Sho winner Shin Tsubame,
then Kikuka Sho winner Matikanefukukitaru, Oka Sho winner Sister Tosho,
4-time G1 winner Special Week and 7-time G1 winner Hall of Famer Vodka.
Still full of vigor since before the war, it's a line that especially shines in the Derby.
11:720: The Astonishment line is counted among Japan's three great female lines with the Flories Cup and Beautiful Dreamer lines.
In 1907, Koiwai Farm in Iwate imported Astonishment from England as a foundation mare.
Since then, the line produced Kurifuji, the great prewar mare, great stayer brothers Mejiro McQueen and Mejiro Durren,
sprinters Shonan Kampf and Trot Star, Oka Sho winners Brocade and Fight Gulliver, Oaks winner Tenmon,
and also Takarazuka Kinen winner Suzu Parade and Tenno Sho winner Offside Trap.
Later came 7-time dirt champion Blue Concorde, Sei Crimson and more - a variety of stars regardless of distance or surface.
11:721: Founder Helen Surf, like Beautiful Dreamer, Astonishment and Flories Cup, was imported to Koiwai Farm in 1907.
This line produced Kikuka Sho winner Akane Tenryu, called the greatest postwar improver, Grand Prix winner Osaichi George,
Hanshin 3yo Stakes winner Katsuragi Haiden, Minami Kanto double winner King Haiseiko, Hishi Miracle, winner of the Kikuka Sho, Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen,
and Meiner Hoou, who won the NHK Mile Cup as 10th favorite.
11:722: Founder S. Sardie was imported from England by Ou Farm in Aomori around 1908.
It produced Tenno Sho winner Nehai Caesar and Yasuda Kinen winner Tsurumaru Boy, among others.
Above all it has produced many dirt champions: unbeaten Minami Kanto Triple Crown winner and JDD winner Toshin Blizzard,
Meisei Opera, the first local horse to win a JRA G1 (February S.), Lively Mount, champion in the first year of dirt exchange races,
and Carib Song, 1990's Best Dirt Horse.
11:723: Founder Craigdarroch was imported from England in 1926 by the state-run Niikappu Imperial Stock Farm.
It produced Tenno Sho winner Aiful among others, and the branch from Corona through Star Roch has been especially remarkable.
From Corona came "star of the lottery horses" Kosei and "child of the hill course" Mihono Bourbon,
and from Star Roch, besides her own Oaks win,
came Satsuki Sho winner Hard Barge, Tenno Sho winner Sakura Yutaka O, double winner Sakura Star O and Derby winner Winning Ticket.
11:724: Founder Tiptop was imported in 1903 by the Hokkaido Livestock Farm.
While most lines descend from English-bred mares, Tiptop was American-bred.
This line produced Asa Denko, who won the Derby amid thunder and lightning,
Merry Nice, who also won the Derby in a romp, and Silk Justice, who won the Arima Kinen as a 3yo.
Stars from great Minami Kanto mare Rosita and Rinnes, of the "City" prefix family, also stand out:
from Rosita came exchange 2-time G1 winner Kanetsu Fleuve and 3-time winner Regular Member,
and from Rinnes came flaxen chestnut G1 winner Gold City and dirt mile champion Espoir City.
11:725: Founder Propontis, like many other lines, was imported from England to Koiwai Farm in 1907.
This line produced Derby winner Ines Fujin, famous for the "Nakano" chant, and Satsuki Sho winner Hakutaisei,
Japan Cup winner Legacy World, 2-time exchange G1 winner Toho Emperor and more.
It also produced many Tokyo Derby winners, such as Sanko Mond, Atomic Thunder and BB Tornado.
11:726: Founder Frustrate, like the three great line founders, was imported from England to Koiwai Farm in 1907.
From her granddaughter Manna came Hall of Famer Tokitsukaze, her sons Derby winner O Tokitsu and Arima Kinen winner Onward There,
and among mares, Tenno Sho winner Cellulose, Arima Kinen and Tenno Sho (Autumn) winner Tomei, Oaks winner Umeno Fiber and more.
This line also produced Hoyo Boy, Horse of the Year in 1980 and 1981, Trot Thunder, unbeaten at a mile,
and Adjudi Mitsuo, local racing's hero with 5 exchange G1 wins including back-to-back Tokyo Daishoten.
11:727: Founder Santa Astra was French-bred and kept in France.
This line's prosperity in Japan began with Amazon Warrior, imported by Mejiro Farm, and Fancimine, imported by Shadai Farm.
From Amazon Warrior came Mejiro Ramonu, Japan's first Fillies' Triple Crown winner, her great-grandson Field Rouge, winner of the Kawasaki Kinen,
and many Mejiro stars like Mejiro Ardan and Mejiro Lambada,
and in 2019, Glory Vase won the Hong Kong Vase.
From Fancimine came Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Admire Max, 3yo mile G1 double winner Rhein Kraft, Kikuka Sho winner Song of Wind,
and recently dirt stars Le Vent Se Leve and Chuwa Wizard.
and overseas, Soviet Star, Black Tie Affair and more.
11:728: Founder Our Lassie was an English-bred Epsom Oaks winner, kept in England.
This line is notable for many horses that succeeded not just as racehorses but as sires.
Overseas: Mill Reef, European Triple Crown winner and hugely successful sire,
5-time G1 winner Blushing Groom, also a hugely successful sire, and Car Red, who went from England to America and spread Hyperion's blood.
In Japan: Fuji Kiseki, Sunday Silence's first G1 winner and a long-successful sire,
and Derby winner King Kamehameha, who became leading sire.
The line also produced Satsuki Sho winner Dyna Cosmos, versatile 6-time G1 winner Agnes Digital,
great sprinter Believe, overseas G1 winner Shadow Gate, Japan Cup Dirt winner Nihon Pillow Hours and more.
11:729: Founder Doxa was born and kept in England.
Her great-granddaughter La Troienne sent many stars to the turf; in Japan, Mejiro Asama, the first grey Tenno Sho winner,
back-to-back Grand Prix winner Mejiro Palmer, Hanshin JF winner T.M. Precure,
Japan Cup winner and successful sire Screen Hero, Nambu Hai winner Arctos, All Japan 2yo Yushun winner Summaries and more.
And the crowning glory is surely unbeaten Triple Crown winner Contrail.
It also produced many Kentucky Derby winners, like Spend a Buck and US near-Triple Crown winner Smarty Jones.
With 5-time G1 mare Stephanie's Kitten, and recently Essential Quality, unbeaten in 3 starts to win the BC Juvenile, and Corniche, it's a line that shines in America too.
11:730: Founder Frizette was American-bred and kept in France.
This line produced historic great sires Tourbillon, Mr. Prospector and US Triple Crown winner Seattle Slew.
Sinndar, winner of the English and Irish Derbies and the Arc, and Rail Link, who beat Deep Impact in the Arc, also come from this line.
Recently too, Coronation Stakes winner Pyledriver, BC Dirt Mile winner Life Is Good and 3-time US turf G1 winner Up to the Mark - its momentum hasn't faded.
In Japan: Tenno Sho winners Let's Go Tarquin and Sakura Chitose O,
QEII Cup winner Sakura Candle, Oaks winner Silk Prima Donna,
Oken Bruce Lee, who won the Kikuka Sho in the shortest time ever after debut, 2-time sprint G1 winner Curren Chan, JBC Sprint winner Taisei Legend and more.
From Tenno Sho winner Heavenly Romance came dirt stars Awardee, Amour Briller and Lani.
Niigata 2yo Stakes winner Lord Quest has two Frizette lines in his female side.
11:731: Founder Pretty Polly was a great mare who won the English Fillies' Triple Crown, kept in England.
She produced Northern Taste, 10-time leading sire in Japan,
and his grandsire, Northern Dancer's sire Nearctic - you could say this line laid the foundation of modern Japanese racing.
In Japan: Katsuragi Ace, the first Japanese-bred Japan Cup winner, Oaks winner Adorable,
sprint stars Masa Lucky and Meiner Love, Tokyo Daishoten winner Star King Man and more.
Recently it has produced dirt star Omega Perfume and Crocosmia, runner-up in the QEII Cup 3 years running.
Overseas: Workforce, who stood in the way of Japanese horses in the Arc,
King George winner Postponed, who brushed aside Duramente in the Dubai Sheema Classic,
and Qualify, who pulled a huge upset as the outsider in the Epsom Oaks.
11:732: Founder Alto Viscar was born and kept in England.
Above all, famous for 7-crown Deep Impact, called the jewel of modern Japanese racing, out of great broodmare Wind in Her Hair.
This branch also produced Derby winner Rey de Oro, Teio Sho winner Gold Blitz, and Regaleira, a filly who won the Hopeful S..
It also produced Take no Velvet, who won the QEII Cup as second-to-last favorite, Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Seiun Kosei and Kikuka Sho winner Durezza,
but its strength in the NHK Mile Cup stands out - starting with inaugural winner Taiki Fortune,
it has produced 3 winners, including Win Kluger and Clarity Sky.
Overseas it produced sires Johannesburg and Tale of the Cat,
Baaeed, unbeaten winner of the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes, BC Turf winner Talismanic and more.
11:733: Founder Fly By Night was an American broodmare.
Her great-great-granddaughter Almahmoud, dam of Halo's dam Cosmah and Northern Dancer's dam Natalma,
is a great broodmare whose name is in pedigrees not just in America but worldwide.
In Japan: Lemon Pop, 2023 spring-autumn dirt champion, Red Rivere, unbeaten Hanshin JF winner, and more.
From branches not via Almahmoud came February S. winner Novo True and
Oi-based Mandarin Hero, a gallant 2nd in the Santa Anita Derby, but there are few big names in Japan.
11:734: Founder Remembrance was an American broodmare whose line flourished at home,
and in Japan, "the Supercar" Maruzensky, imported by Maruzen Hashimoto Farm, shone,
followed by Yasuda Kinen winner Black Hawk and Takarazuka Kinen winner A Shin Deputy.
In France, Vettori won the French 2000 Guineas.
In America, besides US double winner Afleet Alex, it recently produced 2yo G1 winner Bast and Kentucky Derby winner Mage.
11:735: Founder Tobenhau produced no standout herself, but this line produced unbeaten English Triple Crown winner Nijinsky, English and Irish Derby winner The Minstrel,
Spinning World, the great miler of the 1990s who won the Jacques le Marois twice,
and Rags to Riches, a filly who won the Belmont Stakes.
The line flourished in Japan too - especially, there are very many broodmares descending from Best in Show.
QEII Cup winner Fusaichi Pandora is a great-granddaughter,
and her daughter Almond Eye, a Fillies' Triple Crown winner and more, has established herself as one of history's greatest mares.
11:736: Founder St. Lucre was English-bred and kept in France.
She produced many top horses across Europe.
Daltawa especially was a great mare who produced two European Horses of the Year, Daylami and Dalakhani, and G1 winners Dolniya, Dalkala and more followed.
Pay the Butler, who beat Oguri Cap, Tamamo Cross and Tony Bin in the 1988 Japan Cup, is from this line too.
Dubawi, one of the few heirs of great Dubai Millennium, is extending the sire line in Europe.
Prince of Penzance, the huge outsider who won the Melbourne Cup where Japan's Fame Game and Hokko Brave ran, also carries this blood.
In Japan: 10-time dirt G1 winner Hokko Tarumae, QEII Cup winner Little Amapola, Asahi Hai FS winner Jantar Mantar and more.
11:737: Founder Affection was French-bred, but brought to America when WWI halted French racing.
The line from her daughter Escutcheon is the main branch today.
In Japan: Fillies' Triple Crown winner Apapane and her daughter Akaitorino Musume, plus To the Victory, Marcellina, Erimo Chic, Ayusan and more.
Overseas: Nathaniel won the King George, Free Eagle won the Prince of Wales's Stakes where Japan's Spielberg ran,
plus speedy mare Lady Aurelia and stamina-rich Search for a Song, back-to-back Irish St Leger winner.
11:738: Founder Simon's Shoes was born in England in 1914 and kept there.
Especially famous is the Rough Shod branch - in England, Ireland, France and elsewhere,
it produced Sadler's Wells, a legendary sire who was leading sire 17 times in total, and great sire Nureyev -
a line with an enormous influence on modern racing.
The Rough Shod branch also produced Blame, who ended Zenyatta's streak in the BC Classic.
In Japan: El Condor Pasa, the first Japan-trained horse to finish 2nd in the Arc,
Victoria Mile winner Asian Winds, dirt star Gold Dream and more.
Outside Rough Shod, it produced Miss Onward, who won 8 straight including the Oka Sho and Oaks double.
11:739: Founder Boudoir was exported to America in 1942 and was a huge success.
This line produced Bowl of Flowers, US 3yo filly champion and Hall of Famer,
and Majestic Prince, the first in US history to win the double unbeaten, who also succeeded as a sire.
Songbird, who romped in the 2015 BC Juvenile Fillies, won 11 straight unbeaten.
With Beholder, who ended that streak, she made her name as a great mare of recent American racing.
11:740: This line, founded by English broodmare Strenkiss, spread widely through two daughters: Kiss Again, who went to America,
and Straight Lace, who stayed in Europe.
Kiss Again's branch produced Dancing Brave, Europe's best horse of the 1980s,
and in Japan, Delta Blues, winner of the Kikuka Sho and Melbourne Cup, Pixie Knight, who won the Sprinters S. as a 3yo,
Asahi Hai FS winner Do Deuce and more.
Straight Lace herself won the Epsom Oaks and succeeded as a broodmare.
This branch produced Stravinsky, Europe's champion sprinter and a sire,
Magical, who fought epic duels with Enable, and Auguste Rodin, a Deep Impact son who won the English and Irish Derbies.
In Japan it produced Oaks winner Nouvelle Recolte, JBC Classic winner Mutually and more.
11:741: Founder Fruitful was an English broodmare, but the Skylarking branch four generations later was a big success in America.
Devil's Bag, known as Taiki Shuttle's sire, and his brother Saint Ballado, who sired two US Horses of the Year,
great mare Serena's Song, Rahy, sire of 2-time WRC winner Fantastic Light, and Singspiel, winner of the Dubai WC and Japan Cup.
In Japan: back-to-back Grand Prix winner Grass Wonder, record-setting NHK Mile Cup winner Danon Shanty, dominant JBC Ladies' Classic winner White Fugue and more.
Great mare Halwa Sweet produced 3 G1-winning siblings: back-to-back Victoria Mile winner Verxina, Japan Cup winner Cheval Grand and Dubai Turf winner Vivlos.
It also produced BC Turf winner Kalanisi, French leading sire Kaldoun,
and in Japan, "Mile Queen" North Flight and more.
11:742: A line founded by American-bred broodmare Artless.
The Sunny Vale branch produced Kentucky Derby winner Monarchos, US champion turf male Sunshine Forever,
and successful sire Dynaformer, and in Japan, great sire Brian's Time has shone.
Great broodmare I Dreamed a Dream produced double winner Air Shakur and Air Deja Vu, 3rd-2nd-3rd in the fillies' Classics.
Stars keep coming from Air Deja Vu's daughter, Shuka Sho winner Air Messiah.
The Legendra branch is famous for America's great mare Zenyatta, plus Koiuta, Goshawk Ken, Queen Spumante, Let's Go Donki and more.
Recently it produced Stella Veloce, 3rd-3rd-4th in the colts' Classics.
This line has long roots in Japan too - from the branch of Takahata, who fought colts on even terms after the war, came Tenno Sho winner Inglandire and others.
11:743: A great female line founded by English broodmare Paraffin Lass.
In Europe it produced Whistler, a sire of 1960s stars, and American-bred speedster Mummy's Pet.
In America: Crafty Prospector, known as Agnes Digital's sire,
Preakness winner Master Derby, and recently Game On Dude.
Meanwhile, the branch from broodmare Sunny Gulf produced Dubai World Cup winner Street Cry and European champion 2yo Shamardal,
and in Japan, double winner Neo Universe, Oaks winners Lady Pastel and Erin Court, Champions Cup winner T.O. Keynes and more.
When Ballet Queen, daughter of dominant Epsom Oaks winner Sun Princess, was imported to Japan,
her branch produced Derby winner Fusaichi Concorde, Satsuki Sho winners Unrivaled and Victory, and more.
Other branches also produced Satsuki Sho winner Epoca d'Oro, British Champions Sprint winner Creative Force,
and Fillies' Mile winner Pretty Gorgeous - showing real depth in recent years.
11:744: One of America's great female lines, producing not just racehorses but many great sires and mares.
Royal Academy II, who sired stars worldwide, his nephew, great US sire Storm Cat,
Majestic Light, known as Oka Sho winner Nishino Flower's sire, and Be My Guest, English and Irish leading sire.
Also Kentucky Derby winner Fusaichi Pegasus, Pine Bluff, Ice Capade, Coronado's Quest, Uncle Mo,
and NY Fillies' Triple Crown winner Ruffian - countless star mares too.
In Japan: Triple Crown winner Orfevre and his brother, back-to-back Grand Prix winner Dream Journey, Asahi Hai FS winner Satono Ares and more.
11:745: A female line descending from 1983 Oaks winner Dyna Carle.
The standout is surely Air Groove, who achieved a dam-daughter Oaks double and was the first mare in 17 years to win the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
Air Groove produced many graded winners, like QEII Cup winner Admire Groove and QEII Cup (HK) winner Rulership.
Admire Groove then produced Duramente, Satsuki Sho and Derby double winner, continuing a bloodline strong on the big stage.
It also produced siblings Egao wo Misete, a 2-time graded winner, and Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Orewa Matteruze,
and 4-time graded winner I'm Yours - one of Japan's great female lines of recent times.
It's especially known for producing many star mares.
11:746: Founder Scarlet Ink was imported from America in 1973 by Japan's Shadai Group.
With great sire Northern Taste, she produced two graded winners, Scarlet Ribbon and Scarlet Bouquet.
In her grandchildren's generation came Daiwa Scarlet, the first mare in 37 years to win the Arima Kinen, never finishing outside the top 2,
Daiwa Major, a huge success as a sire too, and Vermilion, winner of 9 G1-level races.
Brave Smash won 2 G1s after moving to Australia and went to stud there - the blood has spread worldwide.
Producing varied stars regardless of distance or surface, it's called one of modern Japan's representative female lines.
11:747: Founder Santa Luciana was a German broodmare.
When Irish-born Subtle Change was imported to Japan, she produced 3-time G1 winner Manhattan Cafe.
Notable is her granddaughter Biwa Heidi, born from an in-foal import.
She won the Hanshin JF herself, and as a dam produced Horse of the Year and 6-time G1 winner Buena Vista, Hanshin JF winner Joie de Vivre and six graded winners in all,
11:748: A female line founded by American broodmare Dinner Partner.
Her granddaughter Fabulous Jane produced turf-and-dirt G1 winner Eagle Cafe,
and granddaughter Key Partner produced Tenno Sho winner Suzuka Mambo, but most famous is great broodmare Dancing Key, imported from America in 1990.
She produced 3 Classic winners: Oaks winner Dance Partner, Kikuka Sho winner Dance in the Dark and Oka Sho winner Dance in the Mood,
and graded winners in her grandchildren's generation too - the line keeps spreading.
11:749: A female line founded by Antique Value, imported from America to Japan in 1989.
She produced Vega, winner of the Oka Sho and Oaks double, and Vega produced Derby winner Admire Vega and 7-time G1-level winner Admire Don.
Vega's only broodmare daughter, Historic Star, produced Oka Sho winner Harp Star.
11:750: Founder Royal Sash was imported from England to Japan by the Shadai Group.
Known for Soccer Boy, who set the Japanese turf 2000m record, and Stay Gold, who won the Hong Kong Vase and became a great sire.
Besides these two, many stars, like Shonan Pandora, who won the Japan Cup against seasoned colts, belonged to the Dyna Sash branch,
but other branches produced Sprinters S. winner Snow Dragon and more.
11:751: Founder Urban Sea, an American-bred, French-trained mare, won the Arc as 13th favorite.
She also ran in the Japan Cup (8th), so she's familiar to Japanese fans.
11:752: Founder Mejiro Bosatsu won the Asahi Hai 3yo Stakes against strong colts like future Yayoi Sho winner Tama Shuho, and was named 1965's Best 3yo Filly.
A line tied to Mejiro Farm - her daughter Mejiro Nagasaki produced Mejiro Dober, winner of the Oaks and Shuka Sho,
and Mejiro Quincy produced Mejiro Monterey, winner of the AJCC and Copa Republica Argentina against colts,
Mejiro Monterey's grandson Maurice blossomed as an older horse,
achieving 6 G1 wins at home and abroad, including the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Hong Kong Cup.
11:753: Founder Samovar was English-bred, and her line spread mainly in England and Ireland.
In the 1980s came Mtoto, King George winner and 2-time Eclipse Stakes winner,
and in the 1990s Irish double winner Desert King (both went to stud),
but the line's profile has soared since producing Frankel in the 2010s - unbeaten in 14 starts, hailed as "Europe's greatest ever."
In Japan, broodmare Skia, imported by Shadai Farm, produced siblings Vin de Garde, Fuji Stakes winner, and Satsuki Sho winner Sol Oriens.
11:754: Founder Friar's Carse was American-bred, named US champion 2yo filly on the track.
At stud she produced War Relic, who later spread the Man o' War line as a sire.
Since then, it produced great stayer Order of St George in Europe,
and Belmont Stakes winner Hail to All and 2-time G1 winner Cetewayo in America, but no superstars.
In Japan it has shown good compatibility with the SS line, producing Hong Kong Mile winner Hat Trick, 3-time G2 winner Sunrise Pegasus and more.
It has produced many dirt stars too: 6-time graded winner Agnes Jedi, Funabashi's great mare Lovely Frigg, and above all Copano Rickey, with 11 dirt G1 wins.
11:755: Founder Djebellica won the Irish Oaks.
In Europe, after Arc winner Bon Mot in her grandchildren's generation, it produced Pluralisme, who later stood in Japan, Epsom Derby winner Dr Devious,
and Mark of Distinction, a rare Man o' War line sire.
Recently, Deep Impact son Saxon Warrior won the 2000 Guineas, delighting Japanese fans.
In Japan, after Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Suzuka Phoenix,
the branch of broodmare Souvenir Gift produced graded winners Presage Lift, Dea Regalo and more.
In Australia too, Pierro shone with 5 G1 wins there.
11:756: This line, descending from founder Reply, produced Canadian Horse of the Year L'Enjoleur, Irish-bred Holy Roman Emperor, who later succeeded as a sire,
and Irish-bred Charm Spirit, a 3-time mile G1 winner including the Prix du Moulin.
In Australia, Flying Spur shone in the sprint division in the '90s.
In Japan, besides El Way Win, who beat Biwa Hayahide by a nose in the Asahi Hai 3yo Stakes,
broodmare Croupier Lady's branch produced Satsuki Sho winner Genuine and Asakusa Kings,
but there have been no notable stars recently.
11:757: Founder Portage was an American horse who did little on the track but blossomed as a broodmare.
As the line grew, it produced great US sire Cozzene in the 1980s and Timber Country, imported to Japan as a sire, in the 1990s.
In Europe it produced Dubai Millennium, still named as a candidate for best ever,
followed by French Derby winner Intello, 4-time mile G1 winner Ribchester and more.
In Japan it produced Century's End Emperor T.M. Opera O, Oka Sho winner Reginetta, Asahi Hai FS winner Asia Express,
2-time graded winner Tsurumaru Tsuyoshi and more, but no notable stars recently.
11:758: Founder Margarethen was an American horse who raced a tough 64 times, including a win in the Margate Handicap.
At stud, her daughter Trillion finished 2nd in G1 races 10 times, including the Arc, and was named US champion turf mare.
Trillion produced Triptych, the "Iron Lady" with 9 G1 wins,
and Treve, back-to-back Arc winner and a great of recent times, plus Sprint Cup winner Tamarisk.
In Japan it produced Furioso, dirt champion with 6 G1 wins.
Other branches produced Generous, the great Irish horse of the 1990s, Imagine, winner of the Irish 1000 Guineas and Epsom Oaks,
and Hong Kong's Bullish Luck, who won the Yasuda Kinen.
In Japan too it produced Takarazuka Kinen winner Mikki Rocket, Satsuki Sho winner Dee Majesty, Sprinters S. winner Tower of London and more,
forming a great female line to this day.
11:759: Founder Lady Be Good was an American horse with 4 wins from 13, including the Colleen Stakes.
Most familiar to Japanese fans are Goodbye Halo, the great US mare with 7 G1 wins including the Kentucky Oaks,
and her son King Halo, part of the 1998 Classic generation.
Of course many stars came from other branches too:
in the 1980s, Russian Rubles, a sire imported to Japan (sire of Isono Rouble),
France's Polish Precedent, who won 7 straight in the mile division including 2 G1s (sire of Pilsudski),
and English Horse of the Year Zilzal.
In the 2000s it produced Motivator, Epsom Derby winner and Horse of the Year, who sired back-to-back Arc winner Treve.
Recently it produced BC Filly & Mare Sprint winner Finest City
and Gilded Mirror, who beat future dirt king Lemon Pop by a nose in the Musashino Stakes.
11:760: Founder Mumtaz Mahal was an English horse.
On the track she showed overwhelming speed, winning the 1000m Nunthorpe Stakes by 6 lengths,
Her own foals weren't stars, but this line went on to produce great sires called founders of lines, such as Mahmoud, Royal Charger and Nasrullah.
Later came Shergar, winner of the English and Irish Derbies and King George, Risen Star, winner of the Preakness and Belmont, and Alamshar, winner of the Irish Derby and King George.
In the 2010s it produced Golden Horn, winner of the Epsom Derby and Arc, and Cracksman, 4-time G1 winner including the Champion Stakes.
In Japan, from NHK Cup winner Rugby Ball long ago, to Smart Falcon and Tanino Gimlet, and recently 3-time G1 winner Titleholder.
Today it's harder to find a thoroughbred without Mumtaz Mahal's blood,
and some call her "the mother of speed racing" and "the mother of the modern thoroughbred."
11:761: Founder Lady Pitt won 10 from 47, including the CCA Oaks.
This line shines in America: in the 1980s, BC Sprint winner Dancing Spree,
in the 2000s, 2-time G1 winner Good Reward, and in the 2010s, BC Juvenile Turf winner Oscar Performance.
Then in 2021, Flightline appeared out of nowhere and swept American racing in no time.
Unbeaten in 6 including the BC Classic, all won easily without the whip, he's named with Frankel as a candidate for best ever,
and he greatly raised this line's profile.
There are no notable stars in Japan.
11:762: This line shines in Europe, and the first name that comes up is "the horse of God," European Triple Crown winner Lammtarra.
Great broodmare Korveya produced Hector Protector, European champion 2yo who stood in Japan,
Shanghai, who also stood in Japan, and Bosra Sham, European champion 3yo filly - three siblings.
Later, in the 2000s, it produced Ciro, a 3-time G1 winner including the Prix Lupin, and fellow Lupin winner Act One.
In the 2010s it produced Epsom Derby winner Pour Moi and 2yo G1 winner Ultra.
Meanwhile it has few stars in Japan - Ibuki Perceive, 2nd in the Oka Sho, is about the only standout.
11:763: Founder Two Bob raced a tough 94 times in America, winning 12. The line divides into branches from Two Bob: Twosy, Two Lea and Miz Clementine.
Twosy was her first foal, and from her came Chris Evert, NY Fillies' Triple Crown winner and US Hall of Famer, Winning Colors, a filly who won the Kentucky Derby,
and sire Chief's Crown, US champion 2yo colt. In Japan it produced Tap Dance City, who romped in a sloppy Japan Cup.
Two Lea produced US double winner Tim Tam, and in Japan, Seiun Sky, winner of the Satsuki Sho and Kikuka Sho.
Miz Clementine's branch shines in Japan,
producing Stayers Stakes winner Inter Flag, 2-time graded winner Aloha Dream and 4-time dirt G1 winner Utopia.
11:764: The standout of this line, descending from founder Lacka, is surely Native Dancer.
Winning 21 of 22 (his only defeat in the Kentucky Derby), called "the Grey Ghost," he was popular all over America.
It also shines in America: Bold Lad, US champion 2yo colt who stood in Japan,
and Adjudicating, a 2-time US G1 winner who stood in Japan and succeeded so well he was called "the Sunday Silence of Minami Kanto."
In Europe it produced sire Sovereign Dancer, who sired many stars, and French 3-time G1 winner Priolo, including the Jacques le Marois.
In Japan: Dyna Letter, who ran well on turf or dirt, Oi's Dollar Arabian, and recently Etario, 2nd in the Kikuka Sho.
11:765: Founder It's a Bet won 10 of 34 in America.
Since 2000 it has produced many stars mainly in Europe: Irish 6-time G1 winner Giant's Causeway, "the Iron Horse,"
French Dansili, who later sired Arc winner Rail Link, and Cacique, who raced in France and the US.
In the 2010s it produced Irish 4-time G1 winner Gleneagles and 3-time G1 winner Decorated Knight.
In America, Brazilian-bred Leroidesanimaux was 2005 US champion turf male.
In Japan, 1999 Queen Stakes winner Air Zion was about the only standout, until Phantom Thief won the 2023 Kyodo News Hai.
11:766: Founder Nowhere was an American horse who won 5 of 19, including the Spinaway Stakes.
What spread this line's name worldwide was surely Miesque, Europe's mile queen of the late 1980s.
After 10 G1 wins including back-to-back BC Miles, as a dam she produced great sire Kingmambo, who founded a major line.
Her second foal, East of the Moon, also won the French fillies' double.
Stars have kept coming to this day: Japan-bred French horse Karakontie, BC Mile winner, Deep Impact son and French Derby winner Study of Man,
and Good Baba shone in Hong Kong too.
In Japan, when two broodmares, Loves Only Me and Personal Legend, were imported, the line expanded rapidly.
Loves Only Me produced Dubai Turf winner and sire Real Steel, then Loves Only You won the BC Filly & Mare Turf.
Personal Legend's first foal Miracle Legend won 4 dirt graded races, and her second, Roman Legend, won the Tokyo Daishoten.
From another mare line came Sprinters S. winner Lugal. The Nowhere line is one to watch in recent Japanese racing.
